ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, two light springs with original lengths of $L_{1}{=}10\mathrm{cm}$ and $L_{2}{=}20\mathrm{cm}$, and spring constants of $k_{1}{=}50\mathrm{N/m}$ and $k_{2}{=}20\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$, respectively, are vertically suspended from the ceiling. Between the two springs, there is an object with a mass of $m_{1}{=}0.1\mathrm{kg}$, and at the bottom, another object with a mass of $m_{2}{=}0.2\mathrm{kg}$ is hanging. The entire system is in a state of equilibrium.

1. At this moment, what is the total length of the two springs?
2. If a plate with mass $M$ is used to slowly lift the object below vertically upward until the total length of the two springs equals the sum of their original lengths, determine the magnitude of the pressure exerted by the upper object $m_{2}$ on the plate.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows two light springs vertically connected in series below the ceiling. The upper spring is marked k1 and is connected between the ceiling and the middle block m1; the lower spring is marked k2 and is connected between m1 and the bottom block m2. Therefore the structure is: ceiling—spring k1—block m1—spring k2—block m2. If a supporting plate is used to slowly lift the lower block upward, then the supporting plate is in contact with the bottom block m2. Then reason: take g=10 m/s^2. When initially at rest, the lower spring k2 only bears the gravity of m2, so k2 x2 = m2 g, x2 = 0.2×10/20 = 0.10 m = 10 cm. The upper spring k1 bears the total gravity of m1 and m2, so k1 x1 = (m1+m2)g, x1 = 0.3×10/50 = 0.06 m = 6 cm. The sum of the natural lengths of the two springs is L1+L2=10 cm+20 cm=30 cm, therefore the initial total length of the two springs is 30 cm+6 cm+10 cm=46 cm. When the supporting plate slowly lifts upward until the total length of the two springs is equal to the sum of their natural lengths, let the signed elongations of the upper and lower springs be x1 and x2 respectively, then x1+x2=0. For the force balance of m1: k1 x1 - k2 x2 = m1 g. Substituting x2=-x1 gives (k1+k2)x1=m1g, so x1=0.1×10/(50+20)=1/70 m, x2=-1/70 m. For the force balance of m2, let the supporting force of the supporting plate on m2 be N, then N + k2 x2 = m2 g, therefore N=m2g-k2x2=0.2×10 - 20×(-1/70)=2+2/7≈2.29 N. According to Newton's third law, the magnitude of the pressure of m2 on the supporting plate is also 2.29 N.

method.method_draft: Direct free-body-force method. First read the diagram as a vertical series: ceiling--spring k1--block m1--spring k2--lower block m2; the later plate contacts the lower block m2. For the initial equilibrium, draw FBDs: the lower spring supports only m2, so k2 x2 = m2 g; the upper spring supports m1 plus m2, so k1 x1 = (m1+m2)g. Add the natural lengths L1+L2 to x1+x2 to get the initial total spring length. For the lifted final state, define signed elongations x1 and x2 of the upper and lower springs. The condition that the total length equals the sum of natural lengths gives x1+x2=0. The FBD of m1 gives k1 x1 - k2 x2 = m1 g, and the FBD of m2 with plate normal N gives N + k2 x2 = m2 g. Solve these equations, then use Newton's third law: the force exerted by m2 on the plate has magnitude N.

先描述图像：图中显示天花板下方竖直串联两个轻弹簧，上方弹簧标为 k1，连接在天花板和中间物块 m1 之间；下方弹簧标为 k2，连接在 m1 与底部物块 m2 之间。因此结构为：天花板—弹簧 k1—物块 m1—弹簧 k2—物块 m2。若用托板慢慢向上托起下方物块，则托板接触的是底部物块 m2。

再推理：取 g=10 m/s^2。初始静止时，下方弹簧 k2 只承受 m2 的重力，所以 k2 x2 = m2 g，x2 = 0.2×10/20 = 0.10 m = 10 cm。上方弹簧 k1 承受 m1 和 m2 的总重力，所以 k1 x1 = (m1+m2)g，x1 = 0.3×10/50 = 0.06 m = 6 cm。两弹簧原长之和为 L1+L2=10 cm+20 cm=30 cm，因此初始两弹簧总长为 30 cm+6 cm+10 cm=46 cm。

托板缓慢上托到两弹簧总长等于原长之和时，设上、下弹簧的有符号伸长量分别为 x1、x2，则 x1+x2=0。对 m1 受力平衡：k1 x1 - k2 x2 = m1 g。代入 x2=-x1，得 (k1+k2)x1=m1g，所以 x1=0.1×10/(50+20)=1/70 m，x2=-1/70 m。对 m2 受力平衡，托板对 m2 的支持力为 N，则 N + k2 x2 = m2 g，因此 N=m2g-k2x2=0.2×10 - 20×(-1/70)=2+2/7≈2.29 N。根据牛顿第三定律，m2 对托板的压力大小也为 2.29 N。

method.method_draft: Internal spring-force method. From the diagram, treat each spring force as a transmitted internal force along the vertical chain. Initially, call the lower spring force T2 and the upper spring force T1. Since m2 hangs from the lower spring, T2=m2 g; since the upper spring supports the whole chain below it, T1=(m1+m2)g. Convert forces to elongations by x1=T1/k1 and x2=T2/k2, then add them to L1+L2 for the total initial length. For the final lifted configuration, solve directly for the signed spring forces rather than displacements: the zero-total-extension condition is T1/k1 + T2/k2 = 0, allowing T2 to be negative if the lower spring is compressed. The equilibrium of the middle block is T1 - T2 = m1 g. After finding T2, balance the lower block: N + T2 = m2 g, so N=m2 g - T2. This N is also the magnitude of the pressure/contact force exerted by m2 on the plate.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中天花板下方竖直悬挂两根轻弹簧，上方弹簧标为 k1，下端连接物块 m1；m1 下方再连接下方弹簧 k2；k2 下端悬挂物块 m2。整体是一条竖直串联系统，m1 位于两弹簧之间，m2 位于最下方。

推理：按题设方法，把弹簧力看作竖直链中的内力。初始平衡时，下弹簧只承受下方物块 m2 的重力，所以 T2 = m2 g。上弹簧承受 m1 与 m2 的总重力，所以 T1 = (m1 + m2)g。取 g = 10 m/s^2，则 T2 = 0.2 × 10 = 2 N，T1 = (0.1 + 0.2) × 10 = 3 N。对应伸长量为 x1 = T1/k1 = 3/50 = 0.06 m = 6 cm，x2 = T2/k2 = 2/20 = 0.10 m = 10 cm。两弹簧原长和为 L1 + L2 = 10 cm + 20 cm = 30 cm，所以初始总长度为 30 cm + 6 cm + 10 cm = 46 cm。

最终缓慢上托 m2，使两弹簧总长度等于原长之和，因此总伸长量为零。设弹簧力允许带符号，下弹簧若受压则 T2 为负。由零总伸长条件：T1/k1 + T2/k2 = 0。对中间物块 m1 平衡：T1 - T2 = m1 g = 1 N。代入 k1 = 50 N/m，k2 = 20 N/m，有 T1/50 + T2/20 = 0，即 2T1 + 5T2 = 0，所以 T1 = -2.5T2。再由 T1 - T2 = 1，得 -2.5T2 - T2 = 1，故 T2 = -1/3.5 = -0.286 N。对下方物块 m2 平衡：N + T2 = m2g，所以 N = m2g - T2 = 2 - (-0.286) = 2.286 N ≈ 2.29 N。该 N 即 m2 对托板的压力大小。

推理：按题设方法，把弹簧力看作竖直链中的内力。初始平衡时，下弹簧只承受下方物块 m2 的重力，所以 T2 = m2 g。上弹簧承受 m1 与 m2 的总重力，所以 T1 = (m1 + m2)g。取 g = 10 m/s^2，则 T2 = 0.2 × 10 = 2 N，T1 = (0.1 + 0.2) × 10 = 3 N。对应伸长量为 x1 = T1/k1 = 3/50 = 0.06 m = 6 cm，x2 = T2/k2 = 2/20 = 0.10 m = 10 cm。两弹簧原长和为 L1 + L2 = 10 cm + 20 cm = 30 cm，所以初始总长度为 30 cm + 6 cm + 10 cm = 46 cm。

最终缓慢上托 m2，使两弹簧总长度等于原长之和，因此总伸长量为零。设弹簧力允许带符号，下弹簧若受压则 T2 为负。由零总伸长条件：T1/k1 + T2/k2 = 0。对中间物块 m1 平衡：T1 - T2 = m1 g = 1 N。代入 k1 = 50 N/m，k2 = 20 N/m，有 T1/50 + T2/20 = 0，即 2T1 + 5T2 = 0，所以 T1 = -2.5T2。再由 T1 - T2 = 1，得 -2.5T2 - T2 = 1，故 T2 = -1/3.5 = -0.286 N。对下方物块 m2 平衡：N + T2 = m2g，所以 N = m2g - T2 = 2 - (-0.286) = 2.286 N ≈ 2.29 N。该 N 即 m2 对托板的压力大小。

method.method_draft: Energy/minimum-potential method. Interpret the image as two light springs in series with m1 at the junction and m2 at the lower end. For the initial hanging state, choose signed elongations x1 and x2. Write the potential energy of the unconstrained two-coordinate system as spring energy minus gravitational potential decrease; minimizing with respect to x1 and x2 gives x1=(m1+m2)g/k1 and x2=m2 g/k2, hence the initial total length is L1+L2+x1+x2. For the final slow-lift state, the plate fixes the lower end so that x1+x2=0. Since the lower block's height is fixed by the plate at the final instant, minimize the energy of the spring-m1 subsystem under x2=-x1: U=1/2 k1 x1^2 + 1/2 k2 x2^2 - m1 g x1. This gives (k1+k2)x1=m1 g and x2=-x1. Then find the plate normal from the lower block force balance, N=m2 g - k2 x2, and identify this as the force m2 exerts on the plate.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中天花板下竖直悬挂两根轻弹簧，上方弹簧标为 k1，下方弹簧标为 k2；物块 m1 位于两根弹簧之间，物块 m2 挂在下方弹簧的末端。因此可把系统看成两根竖直串联弹簧，中间连接 m1，底端连接 m2。
再推理：取弹簧向下伸长为正，伸长量分别为 x1, x2。初始平衡可由势能最小得到：U = 1/2 k1 x1^2 + 1/2 k2 x2^2 - (m1+m2)g x1 - m2 g x2。对 x1, x2 分别求极小，得 k1 x1 = (m1+m2)g，k2 x2 = m2 g。取 g = 10 m/s^2，则 x1 = (0.1+0.2)*10/50 = 0.06 m = 6 cm，x2 = 0.2*10/20 = 0.10 m = 10 cm。两弹簧总长为 L1 + L2 + x1 + x2 = 10 cm + 20 cm + 6 cm + 10 cm = 46 cm。
第二问：用板缓慢向上托起下方物块，直到两弹簧总长等于原长之和，所以约束为 x1 + x2 = 0，即 x2 = -x1。此时下端高度由板固定，按指定方法只对弹簧和 m1 子系统写势能：U = 1/2 k1 x1^2 + 1/2 k2 x2^2 - m1 g x1 = 1/2 (k1+k2)x1^2 - m1 g x1。势能最小给出 (k1+k2)x1 = m1 g，所以 x1 = 0.1*10/(50+20) = 1/70 m，x2 = -1/70 m。下方物块 m2 受重力 m2 g 向下、板的支持力 N 向上、下弹簧力大小为 k2|x2| 且因 x2 为压缩而对 m2 向下。对 m2 平衡：N = m2 g - k2 x2 = 0.2*10 - 20*(-1/70) = 2 + 2/7 = 2.2857 N，约为 2.29 N。m2 对板的压力大小等于板对 m2 的支持力大小。

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, two light springs with original lengths of $L_{1}{=}10\mathrm{cm}$ and $L_{2}{=}20\mathrm{cm}$, and spring constants of $k_{1}{=}50\mathrm{N/m}$ and $k_{2}{=}20\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$, respectively, are vertically suspended from the ceiling. Between the two springs, there is an object with a mass of $m_{1}{=}0.1\mathrm{kg}$, and at the bottom, another object with a mass of $m_{2}{=}0.2\mathrm{kg}$ is hanging. The entire system is in a state of equilibrium.

1. At this moment, what is the total length of the two springs?
2. If a plate with mass $M$ is used to slowly lift the object below vertically upward until the total length of the two springs equals the sum of their original lengths, determine the magnitude of the pressure exerted by the upper object $m_{2}$ on the plate.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure shows two light springs vertically connected in series below the ceiling. The upper spring is marked k1 and is connected between the ceiling and the middle block m1; the lower spring is marked k2 and is connected between m1 and the bottom block m2. Therefore the structure is: ceiling—spring k1—block m1—spring k2—block m2. If a supporting plate is used to slowly lift the lower block upward, then the supporting plate is in contact with the bottom block m2.

Then reason: take g=10 m/s^2. When initially at rest, the lower spring k2 only bears the gravity of m2, so k2 x2 = m2 g, x2 = 0.2×10/20 = 0.10 m = 10 cm. The upper spring k1 bears the total gravity of m1 and m2, so k1 x1 = (m1+m2)g, x1 = 0.3×10/50 = 0.06 m = 6 cm. The sum of the natural lengths of the two springs is L1+L2=10 cm+20 cm=30 cm, therefore the initial total length of the two springs is 30 cm+6 cm+10 cm=46 cm.

When the supporting plate slowly lifts upward until the total length of the two springs is equal to the sum of their natural lengths, let the signed elongations of the upper and lower springs be x1 and x2 respectively, then x1+x2=0. For the force balance of m1: k1 x1 - k2 x2 = m1 g. Substituting x2=-x1 gives (k1+k2)x1=m1g, so x1=0.1×10/(50+20)=1/70 m, x2=-1/70 m. For the force balance of m2, let the supporting force of the supporting plate on m2 be N, then N + k2 x2 = m2 g, therefore N=m2g-k2x2=0.2×10 - 20×(-1/70)=2+2/7≈2.29 N. According to Newton's third law, the magnitude of the pressure of m2 on the supporting plate is also 2.29 N.

The upper spring is marked k1 and is connected between the ceiling and the middle block m1; the lower spring is marked k2 and is connected between m1 and the bottom block m2. Therefore the structure is: ceiling—spring k1—block m1—spring k2—block m2. If a supporting plate is used to slowly lift the lower block upward, then the supporting plate is in contact with the bottom block m2.

Then reason: take g=10 m/s^2. When initially at rest, the lower spring k2 only bears the gravity of m2, so k2 x2 = m2 g, x2 = 0.2×10/20 = 0.10 m = 10 cm. The upper spring k1 bears the total gravity of m1 and m2, so k1 x1 = (m1+m2)g, x1 = 0.3×10/50 = 0.06 m = 6 cm. The sum of the natural lengths of the two springs is L1+L2=10 cm+20 cm=30 cm, therefore the initial total length of the two springs is 30 cm+6 cm+10 cm=46 cm.

When the supporting plate slowly lifts upward until the total length of the two springs is equal to the sum of their natural lengths, let the signed elongations of the upper and lower springs be x1 and x2 respectively, then x1+x2=0. For the force balance of m1: k1 x1 - k2 x2 = m1 g. Substituting x2=-x1 gives (k1+k2)x1=m1g, so x1=0.1×10/(50+20)=1/70 m, x2=-1/70 m. For the force balance of m2, let the supporting force of the supporting plate on m2 be N, then N + k2 x2 = m2 g, therefore N=m2g-k2x2=0.2×10 - 20×(-1/70)=2+2/7≈2.29 N. According to Newton's third law, the magnitude of the pressure of m2 on the supporting plate is also 2.29 N.
